findings.text: A device attribute pair exposes AMD L3 subcache partitioning. Reading reports the current subcache setting for the first CPU in the shared map as hexadecimal. Writing requires administrative privilege, interprets input as hexadecimal, applies it through the platform setter for that CPU, and returns the byte count on success with permission or argument errors otherwise.

Private cache attributes stay hidden when cache information lacks private northbridge data. The partitioning attribute appears only when the platform reports partitioning support, and the two index disable attributes appear only when the platform reports index disable support. All other cases remain hidden.

L3 attribute table construction runs once. The first call sizes a table from currently reported features, allocates it, populates entries for index disable and partitioning when present, and publishes it to the shared group. Later calls observe the cached table and do nothing. Allocation failure leaves the group unpublished.

The private group selector returns no group when cache level is below third level or when private data is absent. When a northbridge with computed indices is present it ensures the attribute table is initialized, then returns the shared private group.

The L3 cache initializer declines caches below third level and avoids virtualized use. It resolves the AMD node for the current CPU, looks up the corresponding northbridge, computes L3 index geometry when missing, and returns the northbridge object.
Per CPU frequency samples hold a sequence counter for consistent reads, a timestamp of last update, cached actual and reference deltas, and saved hardware actual and reference counter values.
Hybrid capacity entries hold a normalized capacity value and a frequency ratio value. The subsystem keeps one entry per possible CPU in dynamically allocated per CPU storage.
Turbo and maximum frequency ratios start at the scheduler neutral capacity value. Per CPU frequency scale starts neutral. Both the frequency invariance key and the hybrid capacity key start disabled.

Maximum ratio discovery probes Silvermont style registers first, then Goldmont, Knight family, server, and generic core methods selected by CPU identity tables. Each method extracts base and turbo fields from platform and turbo limit registers. Discovery rejects missing, zero, or inconsistent values including hypervisor zeroed registers, then records the turbo to base proportion scaled to scheduler capacity and updates the maximum ratio with turbo disabled state.

The periodic frequency tick runs only when the aperf mperf feature is present. It reads current hardware actual and reference counters, forms deltas against saved references, updates the saved references, publishes deltas and timestamp under a write sequence section, and invokes the scaler with the deltas.

The scaler does nothing unless invariance is enabled. It rejects shifted actual counts that overflow, scaled reference counts that overflow or are zero, and zero computed scales. It uses the per CPU hybrid ratio when hybrid scaling is enabled else the global maximum ratio, clamps excessive results to neutral capacity, stores the result per CPU, and on anomaly schedules asynchronous disabling.

Boot time invariance setup runs only on Intel and enables the feature under CPU read protection when ratio discovery succeeds. The asynchronous disable path turns off the key and resets every possible CPU scale to neutral. Alternate builds provide empty boot and tick operations that do nothing.

Frequency query for a given CPU retries the sample read until sequence consistent, then validates the reference delta and sample age against the maximum age. Fresh valid samples yield processor base frequency scaled by actual over reference. Stale or invalid samples fall back to the cpufreq quick value when available else the processor base frequency.

Hybrid enable warns and succeeds immediately if already enabled, otherwise allocates per CPU entries, seeds capacity neutral and ratio from the global maximum, enables the key, and reports success. Capacity update scales caller capacity and frequency values by shift then division and warns when not enabled. Capacity query returns stored capacity when enabled else neutral.

Boot initialization checks the aperf mperf feature, captures initial counter references on the boot CPU, and runs invariance boot setup. Application processor initialization captures references on each secondary. A system core resume hook recaptures references after suspend.

Sample updates occur inside a write sequence critical section while queries loop until a consistent sequence read. Boot enabling holds the CPUs read lock. Hybrid and scale state use single access and per CPU accessors to avoid tearing.

Hypervisor identification uses a twelve character signature with two bhyve words separated and followed by a blank. Feature probing uses leaf offset 0x40000001 relative to the discovered base. Extended destination support is indicated by bit zero in that leaf.

Detection requires the hypervisor feature, locates the hypervisor base through the signature helper, caches the maximum leaf, and reports absence as zero. Feature query returns zero when the requested leaf exceeds the cached maximum else the leaf value. Extended destination testing checks the feature bit. Extended APIC availability always reports true. The hypervisor descriptor is named Bhyve and wires detection, noop platform setup, and the two availability callbacks.

Speculation control keeps a global base, a per CPU current value, a per CPU exit to user flag, AMD load store bases and mask, an architectural capability snapshot, a mutex, and a return thunk pointer starting at the default thunk. Six static keys for conditional STIBP, conditional and always IBPB, virtual CPU IBPB, idle buffer clear, and conditional L1D flush all start disabled.

Direct update stores the value per CPU and writes the control register. Conditional update returns early when the per CPU value already matches, otherwise stores the new value and writes the register unless kernel IBRS defers the write to return to user. Current value reading returns the per CPU stored value. Thunk selection updates the global pointer and logs the chosen target.

A dedicated mutex serializes speculation control changes. Core SSB shared disable counting is protected by a raw spinlock. Speculation updates require interrupts disabled with the outer entry saving and restoring interrupt state. Zen sibling handling uses a per CPU test and set bit to prevent reentry on the same CPU.

The update forms the difference between previous and next thread flags, starts from the global base, and selects an SSB method. Virt state writes the virtual register, core state delegates to core handling, and control register methods accumulate into the pending value with converted flag bits. Conditional STIBP is evaluated only on multiprocessor builds when its key is enabled. The pending register is written only when a relevant flag changed.

Non Zen and single variant core handling writes the combined base and converted flag directly. Zen handling tracks a local per CPU enabled bit and a shared disable counter. Enabling sets the local bit once, increments the counter under lock, and writes the masked base only for the first sibling. Disabling clears the local bit once, decrements under lock, and writes the unmasked base only when the last sibling releases.

Guest virtual control handling returns early unless load store or virtual SSB features are present. It derives the host expectation from the global bypass disable state or the current thread flag, masks the guest input to the bypass bit, and when host and guest differ it requests a speculation update using the converted value for the direction being entered.
AMD bypass disabling forces the bypass bit through the virtual register when virtual SSB is present on the boot CPU, otherwise through the load store configuration register combining base and mask.

Mitigation reporting prints enabled attack vectors among user kernel, user user, guest host, and guest guest, followed by the SMT mitigation mode among off, auto, and on. Logging prefixes use mitigations for attack vectors and MDS for memory data sampling sections.

Frequency scaling hazards include shift and multiply overflow, zero divisors, zero computed scales, stale samples from idle or tickless CPUs, and hypervisors that advertise the feature but return zero registers. Any scaling anomaly triggers a warning and asynchronous global disable rather than applying an unreliable value.

Cache attribute handling must tolerate missing private data, absent features, and allocation failure without publishing. Subcache writes must enforce privilege and validate hexadecimal parsing and setter results. Core SSB counting must remain balanced across siblings. Conditional control writes must respect kernel IBRS deferral.
Maximum acceptable sample age equals the kernel tick rate divided by fifty, covering roughly a twenty millisecond window.
